backlog.title: pi-editor-bridge Extension (pi side, TypeScript)
backlog.description: Build the pi TypeScript extension that captures the live AutocompleteProvider via a pass-through addAutocompleteProvider factory, serves it over a Unix domain socket using a JSONL JSON-RPC protocol, and advertises the socket path + auth token to the spawned $EDITOR via process.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE. This is the pi-side component of the two-part bridge architecture.

milestones.title: Extension Foundation & Provider Capture
milestones.description: Create the extension entry point with default factory function, register session_start/session_shutdown lifecycle hooks, and implement the provider capture mechanism via a pass-through addAutocompleteProvider factory. Include a TUI-mode guard since addAutocompleteProvider is a no-op in RPC mode.

tasks.title: Extension entry point, lifecycle hooks & provider capture
tasks.description: Create the main extension file with default export factory, session_start/session_shutdown event registration, and the pass-through addAutocompleteProvider factory that captures the live CombinedAutocompleteProvider into a module-level variable.

subtasks.title: Extension default factory with session_start/session_shutdown lifecycle
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/research-pi-extension-api.md, the extension factory is `(pi: ExtensionAPI) => void | Promise<void>`. The `pi.on()` method is overloaded per-event. Handler signature is `(event, ctx: ExtensionContext) => void | Promise<void>`. Extensions are loaded via jiti (TS works without compile). Per extensions.md: do NOT start background resources in the factory body — defer to session_start.
2. INPUT: The `pi: ExtensionAPI` object passed to the default export.
3. LOGIC: Create `extension/pi-editor-bridge.ts` with a default export function that calls `pi.on("session_start", handler)` and `pi.on("session_shutdown", handler)`. Import types via `import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent"`. The session_start handler should receive `(event: SessionStartEvent, ctx: ExtensionContext)`. For now, just log/console.log a startup message. The session_shutdown handler is a no-op placeholder.
4. OUTPUT: A valid extension file installable at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-editor-bridge.ts` that pi can load without errors. Exports default factory function.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc comment block at top of file documenting purpose, env var name, and socket transport. No external docs yet.

subtasks.title: Provider capture via pass-through addAutocompleteProvider factory
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/research-pi-autocomplete.md, `addAutocompleteProvider` pushes the factory to `autocompleteProviderWrappers[]` and calls `setupAutocompleteProvider()` which re-applies ALL factories in order. The factory receives `current: AutocompleteProvider` (the live chain, at minimum CombinedAutocompleteProvider) and must return an AutocompleteProvider. A pass-through factory that returns `current` unchanged captures the reference with zero behavior change. The `AutocompleteProvider` type is imported from `@earendil-works/pi-tui`. Re-registering on each session_start is safe because setupAutocompleteProvider rebuilds the chain from scratch. NOTE: wrappers are cleared on session reset (interactive-mode.ts:1952), so re-registration on each session_start is REQUIRED.
2. INPUT: `ExtensionContext` from the session_start event handler (specifically `ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider`).
3. LOGIC: Define a module-level variable `let liveProvider: AutocompleteProvider | undefined`. In session_start, call `ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider((current) => { liveProvider = current; return current; })`. Export a `getProvider()` function that returns the captured provider or throws if undefined. Import type: `import type { AutocompleteProvider } from "@earendil-works/pi-tui"`.
4. OUTPUT: `liveProvider` is populated with the live CombinedAutocompleteProvider after session_start. `getProvider()` returns it for use by RPC handlers.
5. MOCKING: In tests, mock `ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider` to verify the factory is called with a provider and that it returns the same provider unchanged.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on `captureProvider()` explaining the pass-through capture technique and why it must be called in session_start.

subtasks.title: TUI mode guard — no-op when ctx.mode !== 'tui'
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/research-pi-extension-api.md, `addAutocompleteProvider` is a NO-OP in RPC mode (rpc-mode.ts:271-273). It only actually layers providers in TUI mode. Also, `openExternalEditor()` is TUI-only — the external editor is never launched in RPC/json/print modes. Therefore the bridge should only activate in TUI mode. `ctx.mode` is typed as `ExtensionMode = "tui" | "rpc" | "json" | "print"`.
2. INPUT: `ctx.mode` from the session_start event handler.
3. LOGIC: At the top of the session_start handler, add `if (ctx.mode !== "tui") return;` to short-circuit all bridge logic. This prevents registering a useless provider capture factory and starting a socket server that will never be connected to.
4. OUTPUT: The extension no-ops entirely in non-TUI modes. No env var set, no socket started.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc comment on the guard explaining the RPC no-op limitation.

tasks.title: IPC protocol shared types
tasks.description: Define the TypeScript types that form the JSON-RPC 2.0 IPC protocol contract between the bridge extension and the Neovim plugin. These types encode the wire format and must match pi's AutocompleteItem/AutocompleteSuggestions exactly.

subtasks.title: Define JSON-RPC envelope, method, and bridge descriptor types
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/research-pi-autocomplete.md, AutocompleteItem is `{ value: string; label: string; description?: string }` and AutocompleteSuggestions is `{ items: AutocompleteItem[]; prefix: string }`. The applyCompletion return type is `{ lines: string[]; cursorLine: number; cursorCol: number }`. The PRD §5 specifies JSON-RPC 2.0 envelopes with string `id`, and methods: hello, ping, getSuggestions, applyCompletion, shouldTriggerFileCompletion, getCommands, commandsChanged (notification), bye.
2. INPUT: pi's AutocompleteItem and AutocompleteSuggestions types from `@earendil-works/pi-tui`.
3. LOGIC: Create `extension/protocol.ts` with: (a) `JsonRpcRequest` — `{ jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string; method: string; params?: unknown }`, (b) `JsonRpcResponse` — `{ jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string; result?: unknown } | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string; error: { code: number; message: string } }`, (c) `JsonRpcNotification` — `{ jsonrpc: "2.0"; method: string; params?: unknown }`, (d) `BridgeDescriptor` — `{ transport: "unix"; path: string; token: string; pid: number; cwd: string; fdAvailable: boolean; serverVersion: string }`, (e) Method name union type and params/result types for each method matching §5.4 table exactly. Re-export AutocompleteItem and AutocompleteSuggestions from pi-tui for convenience.
4. OUTPUT: A `protocol.ts` module importable by the extension that provides full type safety for the IPC layer.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on each type explaining its wire format role.

milestones.title: JSONL Socket Server & RPC Engine
milestones.description: Implement the Unix domain socket server with JSONL framing, connection lifecycle, token-based handshake authentication, and JSON-RPC method handlers that delegate to the captured live provider. Includes per-request timeout and stale-request supersession for cancellation.

tasks.title: Socket server lifecycle (start/stop/idempotent)
tasks.description: Implement startBridge() and stopBridge() functions that manage the Unix domain socket server's lifecycle, token generation, socket file permissions, and environment variable advertisement.

subtasks.title: startBridge() — create Unix socket server, generate token, chmod 0o600
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/external_deps.md, Node builtins available: `node:net` (createServer), `node:crypto` (randomUUID), `node:os` (tmpdir), `node:path` (join), `node:fs` (chmodSync). Per architecture/research-pi-extension-api.md, background resources MUST start in session_start, not factory body. Socket path: `${os.tmpdir()}/pi-editor-bridge-${randomUUID()}.sock`. Token: 32 hex chars from randomUUID. Per PRD §12, socket must have 0o600 permissions.
2. INPUT: `ctx: ExtensionContext` from session_start (for `ctx.cwd`).
3. LOGIC: Create `startBridge(ctx: ExtensionContext)` that: (a) calls `stopBridge()` first for idempotency, (b) generates token via `randomUUID().replace(/-/g, "").slice(0, 32)`, (c) generates socket path via `join(tmpdir(), 'pi-editor-bridge-${randomUUID()}.sock')`, (d) creates `net.createServer(onConnection)` and calls `server.listen(socketPath)`, (e) calls `chmodSync(socketPath, 0o600)` on non-Windows. Store server, socketPath, token in module-level vars. The onConnection callback is a placeholder for now.
4. OUTPUT: `server`, `socketPath`, `token` module-level variables populated. Server listening on the Unix socket.
5. MOCKING: In tests, mock `net.createServer` and verify listen is called with the generated path.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on startBridge() explaining the socket lifecycle, token generation, and permission model.

subtasks.title: stopBridge() — close server, unlink socket, clear state, idempotent
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §6.2, session_shutdown handler must close the server and unlink the socket. Per architecture/research-pi-extension-api.md, session_shutdown reasons include session replacement (new/resume/fork/reload) — cleanup must be idempotent and re-openable on next session_start.
2. INPUT: Module-level `server`, `socketPath`, `token` variables from S5.
3. LOGIC: Create `stopBridge()` that: (a) wraps everything in try/catch for idempotency, (b) calls `server?.close()`, (c) calls `rmSync(socketPath, { force: true })` to unlink the socket file, (d) resets `server`, `socketPath`, `token` to undefined, (e) deletes `process.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE`. Must be safe to call when server is already stopped (all optional chaining + force:true).
4. OUTPUT: All bridge state cleared. Socket file removed. Env var deleted. Safe to call multiple times.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on stopBridge() explaining idempotency requirements across session churn.

tasks.title: JSONL framing & connection handling
tasks.description: Implement the JSONL line reader that buffers partial socket chunks and splits on newline only (never U+2028/U+2029), plus the connection handler that wires incoming data through the reader and dispatches parsed JSON-RPC messages to handlers.

subtasks.title: JSONL line reader — buffer partial lines, split on \n only, strip \r
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/research-pi-extension-api.md (RPC framing rules from rpc.md): use strict JSONL semantics with LF (
) as the ONLY record delimiter. Accept optional 
 by stripping trailing . Do NOT use Node readline (it splits on U+2028/U+2029 which are valid inside JSON strings). Both sides must buffer partial lines and decode on 
.
2. INPUT: Raw string chunks from socket `data` events (may contain partial lines, multiple lines, or complete lines).
3. LOGIC: Create a `JsonlReader` class (or factory) with: (a) an internal `buffer: string`, (b) a `feed(chunk: string)` method that appends to buffer, splits on 
, strips trailing  from each line, JSON.parse each complete line, and calls the registered callback with the parsed object. The last partial segment stays in the buffer. Handle empty lines gracefully (skip).
4. OUTPUT: A `JsonlReader` instance that emits parsed JSON objects via callback, one per complete 
-delimited line.
5. MOCKING: Unit-test with multi-line chunks, partial chunks spanning feed() calls, 
 endings, and empty lines. Verify no U+2028/U+2029 splitting.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc explaining the strict 
-only framing rationale (reference pi rpc.md rules).

subtasks.title: onConnection handler — accept, wire reader, dispatch, write responses
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §5.3, the server must support at least one concurrent connection (multiplex by id). Each connection gets its own JsonlReader. The server tracks per-connection state (handshake completed, etc.). Per PRD §6.5, responses are sent by writing `JSON.stringify(response) + "\n"` back to the socket.
2. INPUT: A `net.Socket` object from the createServer connection callback. The module-level `cwd: string` and `token: string`.
3. LOGIC: Implement `onConnection(sock: Socket, cwd: string)` that: (a) creates a per-connection `ConnectionContext` tracking `{ sock, authenticated: boolean, reader: JsonlReader }`, (b) wires `sock.on("data", (chunk) => reader.feed(chunk.toString("utf-8")))`, (c) the reader callback dispatches to a `handleMessage(connCtx, msg)` function (placeholder for now — just logs), (d) wires `sock.on("error", () => {})` and `sock.on("close", () => {})` for cleanup, (e) provides a `sendResponse(connCtx, obj)` helper that writes `JSON.stringify(obj) + "\n"` to the socket.
4. OUTPUT: Incoming JSON-RPC messages are parsed and dispatched. Responses can be sent back via sendResponse().
5. MOCKING: Mock net.Socket to verify data event wiring and response writing.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on onConnection explaining connection lifecycle and multiplexing.

tasks.title: Handshake & token authentication
tasks.description: Implement the hello handshake that validates the client's token against the server's, replies with server info on success or an error + close on mismatch. Enforce that no RPC methods are accepted before a valid handshake.

subtasks.title: hello handshake — validate token, reply success or error+close
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §5.3, client sends `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"hello","id":"h1","params":{"token":"...","client":"pi-editor.nvim","clientVersion":"..."}}`. Server validates token: on match reply `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"h1","result":{"ok":true,"serverVersion":"...","cwd":"...","fdAvailable":true}}`. On mismatch reply error code -32600 "bad token" then close the socket. Per PRD §12, token is 32-byte random hex delivered via process.env.
2. INPUT: The `hello` request params `{ token, client?, clientVersion? }` from the client. The module-level `token` and `cwd` for comparison and response.
3. LOGIC: In handleMessage, detect method === "hello". Compare `params.token === serverToken`. If match: set `connCtx.authenticated = true`, send success result with `{ ok: true, serverVersion: "0.1.0", cwd, fdAvailable: !!fdPathAvailable() }`. If mismatch: send error `{ code: -32600, message: "bad token" }`, then `sock.destroy()`. The fdAvailable check can use a simple heuristic (check if `fd` binary is in PATH) or always return true initially.
4. OUTPUT: Authenticated connections have `connCtx.authenticated = true` and receive server info. Unauthenticated connections are closed.
5. MOCKING: Test with correct token (success), wrong token (error + close), and missing token (error + close).
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on handshake explaining token validation and security boundary.

subtasks.title: Reject any method before valid handshake
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §12, 'The bridge must reject any method before a valid hello.' This is the security boundary preventing unauthenticated access.
2. INPUT: Any incoming JSON-RPC message on a connection.
3. LOGIC: In handleMessage, before dispatching to RPC handlers, check: if `method !== "hello" && !connCtx.authenticated`, send error `{ code: -32000, message: "not authenticated" }` and return early (do not process).
4. OUTPUT: No RPC methods except `hello` are processed before authentication.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Inline comment documenting the auth gate.

tasks.title: RPC method handlers (delegate to live provider)
tasks.description: Implement all JSON-RPC method handlers that delegate to the captured live AutocompleteProvider: getSuggestions, applyCompletion, shouldTriggerFileCompletion, ping, bye, and getCommands. Each handler wraps the provider call in try/catch and returns JSON-RPC error envelopes on failure.

subtasks.title: getSuggestions handler with AbortController + supersession
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/research-pi-autocomplete.md, `getSuggestions(lines: string[], cursorLine: number, cursorCol: number, options: { signal: AbortSignal; force?: boolean }): Promise<AutocompleteSuggestions | null>`. The provider uses `fd` for fuzzy @file search (async, respects AbortSignal) and `readdirSync` for path completion (sync). Per PRD §5.5, the server creates an AbortController per request and aborts it if a newer request arrives (supersession).
2. INPUT: Request params `{ lines: string[], cursorLine: number, cursorCol: number, force?: boolean }`. The `liveProvider` from `getProvider()` (dependency P1.M1.T1.S2). A module-level `pendingAbort: AbortController | undefined`.
3. LOGIC: Implement `handleGetSuggestions(params, connCtx)`: (a) call `getProvider()` (throws if not captured), (b) abort any pending request via `pendingAbort?.abort()`, (c) create new `const ac = new AbortController(); pendingAbort = ac;`, (d) set a 1500ms timeout via `setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 1500)`, (e) call `await provider.getSuggestions(params.lines, params.cursorLine, params.cursorCol, { signal: ac.signal, force: !!params.force })`, (f) clear timeout, return result. Wrap in try/catch — on error return JSON-RPC error.
4. OUTPUT: Returns `AutocompleteSuggestions | null` as the JSON-RPC result. Stale requests are aborted.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the handler explaining supersession and fd timeout.

subtasks.title: applyCompletion handler
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: `applyCompletion(lines, cursorLine, cursorCol, item: AutocompleteItem, prefix: string)` returns `{ lines: string[]; cursorLine: number; cursorCol: number }`. This is synchronous — no async/await needed.
2. INPUT: Request params `{ lines, cursorLine, cursorCol, item, prefix }`. The `liveProvider`.
3. LOGIC: Call `getProvider().applyCompletion(params.lines, params.cursorLine, params.cursorCol, params.item, params.prefix)` and return the result. Wrap in try/catch.
4. OUTPUT: Returns `{ lines: string[]; cursorLine: number; cursorCol: number }` as the JSON-RPC result.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc noting this is a synchronous delegation.

subtasks.title: shouldTriggerFileCompletion handler
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: `shouldTriggerFileCompletion?` is optional on the provider. It may be undefined. When undefined, default to `true` (matching pi's editor.ts behavior at line 2150-2160). It returns `false` when typing a bare slash command like `/set` at start of line with no space.
2. INPUT: Request params `{ lines, cursorLine, cursorCol }`. The `liveProvider`.
3. LOGIC: Call `getProvider().shouldTriggerFileCompletion?.(params.lines, params.cursorLine, params.cursorCol) ?? true` and return the boolean. Wrap in try/catch.
4. OUTPUT: Returns `boolean` as the JSON-RPC result.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc noting the optional method and default-true behavior.

subtasks.title: ping, bye, getCommands handlers
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §5.4, `ping` returns `{ ok, pid, cwd, fdAvailable, serverVersion }`. `bye` returns `{ ok: true }` and gracefully disconnects. `getCommands` returns `{ commands: CommandInfo[] }` for richer docs menus (optional — can return empty array if provider doesn't expose commands). `commandsChanged` is a server→client notification, not a request.
2. INPUT: Process info (`process.pid`), module-level `cwd`. For getCommands, optionally query the provider for command metadata (if available).
3. LOGIC: (a) ping handler returns `{ ok: true, pid: process.pid, cwd, fdAvailable, serverVersion: "0.1.0" }`. (b) bye handler returns `{ ok: true }` and schedules socket close. (c) getCommands handler returns `{ commands: [] }` (placeholder — can be enriched later, it's optional per PRD).
4. OUTPUT: All three methods return proper JSON-RPC results.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on each handler.

tasks.title: Cancellation, timeout & error wrapping
tasks.description: Ensure all RPC handlers are wrapped in try/catch to return JSON-RPC error envelopes instead of throwing, and that the supersession/timeout logic in getSuggestions is robust.

subtasks.title: Wrap all handlers in try/catch with JSON-RPC error responses
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §6.7, 'Never throws from handlers (wrap in try/catch, return JSON-RPC error)' and 'Never blocks pi's event loop synchronously (all getSuggestions are awaited)'.
2. INPUT: All RPC handler implementations from T6.
3. LOGIC: Create a `wrapHandler(handler)` higher-order function that wraps any async handler in try/catch. On caught error, return `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: req.id, error: { code: -32603, message: error.message } }`. Apply this wrapper in the dispatch logic. Also ensure the 1500ms timeout from S11 properly aborts and returns a clean result (not an unhandled rejection).
4. OUTPUT: No handler ever throws to the caller. All errors become JSON-RPC error envelopes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on wrapHandler explaining the error-boundary contract.

milestones.title: Env Advertisement & Packaging
milestones.description: Wire the bridge descriptor into process.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE so the spawned Neovim inherits it, implement commandsChanged notifications for provider rebuilds, and package the extension for installation.

tasks.title: process.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE advertisement
tasks.description: After starting the socket server, write a single-line JSON descriptor to process.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE with all fields needed by the Neovim plugin to connect.

subtasks.title: Write BridgeDescriptor JSON to process.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/system_context.md, the editor child process inherits process.env because spawn() has no `env` option (interactive-mode.ts:3811-3816). Per PRD §4, the descriptor is: `{"transport":"unix","path":"/tmp/pi-editor-bridge-xxxx.sock","token":"<32 hex>","pid":12345,"cwd":"/home/u/proj","fdAvailable":true,"version":"0.0.1"}`. This is the discovery mechanism that makes the whole design work.
2. INPUT: Module-level `socketPath`, `token`, and `ctx.cwd` from the session_start handler.
3. LOGIC: In startBridge() (or right after it's called), write `process.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE = JSON.stringify({ transport: "unix", path: socketPath, token, pid: process.pid, cwd, fdAvailable: true, serverVersion: "0.1.0" })`. In stopBridge() (already implemented in S6), delete the env var.
4. OUTPUT: `process.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE` contains a valid JSON string that the Neovim child can read via `vim.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE`.
5. MOCKING: Verify the env var is set after startBridge and deleted after stopBridge.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc explaining the process.env inheritance discovery and its criticality.

tasks.title: commandsChanged notification on provider rebuild
tasks.description: When session_start fires with reason reload/new/resume/fork and the server is already running (meaning a client may be connected), broadcast a commandsChanged notification to connected clients so they can clear their caches.

subtasks.title: Broadcast commandsChanged S→C notification on session_start when server running
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §6.2, session_start with reason reload/new/resume/fork re-captures the provider (which may have changed commands). If a client is already connected, it should be notified to clear its command cache. Per PRD §5.4, commandsChanged is a server→client notification (no id, no reply expected): `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"commandsChanged","params":{}}`.
2. INPUT: The list of active authenticated connections. The session_start event reason.
3. LOGIC: After re-capturing the provider in session_start, if `server` is defined (already running), iterate all authenticated connections and send the commandsChanged notification via `sendResponse` (using notification format — no id field). Maintain a `Set<ConnectionContext>` of active connections.
4. OUTPUT: Connected clients receive commandsChanged when commands are rebuilt.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc explaining the reload notification flow.

tasks.title: Extension packaging & README
tasks.description: Create the package.json manifest for the extension, a README documenting installation and configuration, and verify the extension works in both single-file and package layouts.

subtasks.title: Create package.json manifest and README.md
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/research-pi-extension-api.md, extensions can be installed as single files at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/*.ts` or as packages with `package.json` containing `{ "name":"...", "main":"./index.ts", "pi":{ "extensions":["./index.ts"] } }`. The extension uses ONLY Node builtins (net, crypto, fs, os, path) — no npm runtime dependencies.
2. INPUT: The completed extension code from M1 and M2.
3. LOGIC: Create `extension/package.json` with `{ "name": "pi-editor-bridge", "version": "0.1.0", "main": "./index.ts", "pi": { "extensions": ["./index.ts"] }, "dependencies": {} }`. Create `extension/README.md` documenting: what it does, installation (single-file drop-in and pi install), prerequisites (pi with extension support), how to verify (start pi, open editor, check completion works), and known limitations (TUI-only, load-order capture limitation).
4. OUTPUT: Extension is installable via both methods. README is complete.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The README.md IS the documentation for this subtask.

backlog.title: pi-editor.nvim Plugin Core (Neovim side, Lua)
backlog.description: Build the Neovim Lua plugin that activates only when PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE env var is present (i.e., when pi launches Neovim as $EDITOR), connects to the bridge's Unix socket, and renders pi's completion suggestions through a dependency-free floating menu with acceptance delegated back to pi's applyCompletion for byte-identical insertion behavior.

milestones.title: Plugin Scaffold & Activation
milestones.description: Create the plugin directory structure, setup() function with default options, VimEnter auto-activation shim, and the activation gate that reads PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE and decides whether to activate or stay dormant.

tasks.title: Plugin structure, setup() & default options
tasks.description: Create the init.lua module with setup() function accepting user configuration, defining default options for menu dimensions, debounce, RPC timeout, autosave, and completion engine selection.

subtasks.title: init.lua with setup() and default config options
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §7.5 and §10.5, default options: `menu = { max_height = 12, border = "rounded" }`, `debounce_ms = 25`, `rpc_timeout_ms = 2000`, `autosave_on_exit = true`, `engine = "builtin"`. Per architecture/external_deps.md, Neovim 0.10+ required (0.12 verified). Plugin module path is `lua/pi-editor/`.
2. INPUT: User-provided options table (or empty table).
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/lua/pi-editor/init.lua` with a module table `M`. Implement `M.setup(opts)` that merges `opts` over defaults (using `vim.tbl_deep_extend`), stores config in `M.config`, and exposes it for other modules. Also expose `M.bridge` (placeholder nil for now) so external code can access the bridge client per PRD §7.7.
4. OUTPUT: `require("pi-editor").setup({})` works without errors and config is stored.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring (`---@module` annotations) on setup() documenting each option.

subtasks.title: plugin/pi-editor.lua VimEnter auto-activation shim
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §7.1, the plugin reads PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE on VimEnter (once). Files in `plugin/` are auto-sourced by Neovim on startup (before VimEnter if lazy=false). Per architecture/external_deps.md, lazy.nvim config should use `lazy = false` so the plugin loads before VimEnter.
2. INPUT: The setup() config from S19.
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/plugin/pi-editor.lua` that registers a `VimEnter` autocmd. The autocmd callback calls `require("pi-editor").activate()` (to be implemented in S21). This file is auto-sourced on Neovim startup.
4. OUTPUT: On VimEnter, the activate function is called exactly once.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Comment explaining the VimEnter auto-activation and dormant behavior.

tasks.title: Activation gate — read & validate PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE
tasks.description: Implement the activation logic that reads the PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE environment variable, validates the JSON descriptor, checks transport type, and either activates the plugin for the current buffer or stays dormant.

subtasks.title: VimEnter gate — parse env var, validate, activate or stay dormant
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/external_deps.md, `vim.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE` gives the raw string. `vim.json.decode` parses it (may throw — wrap in pcall). Per PRD §7.1, if absent or unparseable → do nothing (dormant). If present and transport == "unix" → activate for the first buffer. The descriptor has fields: transport, path, token, pid, cwd, fdAvailable, serverVersion. Per architecture/system_context.md, there are two temp-file patterns (pi-editor-<ts>.pi.md and pi-extension-editor-<ts>.md); env var alone is sufficient and precise.
2. INPUT: `vim.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE` raw string.
3. LOGIC: Implement `M.activate()` in init.lua: (a) read `vim.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE`, (b) if nil → return (dormant), (c) `pcall(vim.json.decode, raw)` — if fails → return silently (maybe single notify), (d) if `desc.transport ~= "unix"` → return, (e) store descriptor, (f) set buffer-local filetype to "pi-prompt", (g) trigger ftplugin setup (via S22), (h) initiate bridge connection (placeholder — will be wired in M5).
4. OUTPUT: Plugin is activated only when env var is present and valid. Buffer is marked as pi-prompt. Descriptor stored for bridge client use.
5. MOCKING: Test with valid JSON, invalid JSON, missing env var, non-unix transport.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining the dormant-by-design behavior.

tasks.title: ftplugin/pi-prompt.lua buffer setup
tasks.description: Create the ftplugin that configures the pi prompt buffer with appropriate options, buffer-local keymaps for completion navigation and acceptance, and buffer-local autocmds for completion triggers and autosave.

subtasks.title: Buffer-local options, keymaps & autocmds for pi-prompt filetype
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §7.6, buffer setup includes: options (formatoptions-=t, textwidth=0, wrap, spell=false), keymaps (<Tab> trigger/accept, <S-Tab>, <C-N>/<C-P>, <C-E>, <CR> newline or accept), autocmds (InsertEnter/TextChangedI/CursorMovedI → completion refresh; ExitPre/VimLeavePre/BufWriteCmd → autosave; BufWritePre → no-op). Per architecture/external_deps.md, buffer-local autocmds use `vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd(..., { buffer = bufnr })`.
2. INPUT: The current buffer number (0 for current). Config from setup() (S19).
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/ftplugin/pi-prompt.lua` that: (a) sets `vim.bo.formatoptions:remove("t")`, `vim.bo.textwidth = 0`, `vim.wo.wrap = true`, `vim.wo.spell = false`, (b) sets buffer-local keymaps using `vim.keymap.set("i", "<Tab>", ...)` etc., mapping to functions in completion.lua (placeholder callbacks for now), (c) registers buffer-local autocmds for completion triggers (InsertEnter, TextChangedI, CursorMovedI), (d) registers VimLeavePre/ExitPre autocmd for autosave (implementation in S38).
4. OUTPUT: The pi-prompt buffer has correct options, keymaps, and autocmds. Other buffers/windows are unaffected.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Comment block documenting each keymap's purpose and the pi-specific behavior (e.g., CR inserts newline since there's no Enter-to-submit in external editor).

milestones.title: Bridge Client (Lua) — Socket, JSONL, Handshake, RPC
milestones.description: Implement the Lua-side bridge client: JSONL reader, luv Unix socket connection, token handshake, and RPC dispatch with monotonic id correlation and stale-response supersession.

tasks.title: JSONL reader module (Lua)
tasks.description: Implement a Lua module that buffers partial socket chunks and emits parsed JSON objects one per newline-delimited line, mirroring the server-side framing rules.

subtasks.title: jsonlreader.lua — buffer chunks, split on \n, decode each line
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/external_deps.md, `vim.json.decode(str)` parses JSON (throws on invalid — wrap in pcall). The framing rules from rpc.md: split on \n only, strip trailing \r, do NOT use readers that split on U+2028/U+2029. Per PRD §5.2, both sides buffer partial lines.
2. INPUT: String chunks from `pipe:read_start()` callback (may be partial or multi-line).
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/lua/pi-editor/jsonlreader.lua` as a module returning a factory `M.new(on_message)`. Internal state: `buffer = ""`. Method `feed(chunk)` that: (a) appends chunk to buffer, (b) splits buffer on \n, (c) for each complete line (all but last segment): strip trailing \r, skip empty, pcall vim.json.decode, call on_message(parsed) on success, (d) keep last partial segment in buffer.
4. OUTPUT: Each call to `feed(chunk)` results in zero or more `on_message(table)` callbacks for complete JSON lines.
5. MOCKING: Test with multi-line, partial-across-feeds, \r\n, empty lines. Verify no U+2028 splitting.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining strict \n-only framing.

tasks.title: Socket client & handshake
tasks.description: Implement the bridge.lua module that connects to the Unix socket via luv, performs the token handshake, and wires incoming data through the JSONL reader.

subtasks.title: bridge.lua connect() — luv pipe, read_start, write helper
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/external_deps.md, `vim.uv.new_pipe(false)` creates a non-IPC pipe. `pipe:connect(path, callback)` connects. `pipe:read_start(callback)` starts reading (callback receives `(err, chunk)` where chunk=nil means EOF). `pipe:write(data, callback)` writes. `pipe:close()` closes.
2. INPUT: Socket path from the descriptor, the JSONL reader module from S23.
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/lua/pi-editor/bridge.lua` with `M.connect(path, token, on_ready, on_event)`. Create pipe, wire `read_start` to feed the JsonlReader, implement `M.send(obj)` that writes `vim.json.encode(obj) .. "\n"`. On connect error, call `on_ready(err)`. On EOF, handle gracefully.
4. OUTPUT: A connected pipe with data flowing through the JSONL reader to on_event callbacks. on_ready called on successful connect.
5. MOCKING: Test connect success/failure, verify write format.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring on connect() explaining the luv pipe lifecycle.

subtasks.title: hello handshake — send token, validate response, extract server info
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §5.3, client sends hello immediately after connect: `{ jsonrpc:"2.0", id:"h1", method:"hello", params:{ token:token, client:"pi-editor.nvim", clientVersion:"0.1.0" } }`. Server replies success or error. Per PRD §5.4, success result is `{ ok:true, serverVersion:"...", cwd:"...", fdAvailable:true }`.
2. INPUT: The token from the descriptor, the bridge.send() from S24.
3. LOGIC: After successful connect, send the hello request. Set up a one-time handler for id "h1": if result.ok is true, store serverVersion/cwd/fdAvailable, call on_ready(nil, serverInfo). If error, call on_ready(error_message). Add a timeout (e.g., 3000ms) — if no hello response, call on_ready("handshake timeout").
4. OUTPUT: On success, bridge is authenticated and server info is available. On failure, on_ready is called with an error.
5. MOCKING: Test with success response, error response, timeout.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining the handshake protocol.

tasks.title: RPC dispatch with id correlation & supersession
tasks.description: Implement the request/response correlation layer that auto-assigns monotonic ids, tracks pending requests, and drops responses whose id is not the current pending request (natural supersession/cancellation).

subtasks.title: request(method, params, cb) with auto-id, correlation, stale drop
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §5.5, the client should 'simply supersede stale requests: when a new keystroke arrives, increment id, ignore any response whose id is not the latest.' The RPC timeout is configurable (default 2000ms). Per architecture/external_deps.md, responses are correlated by string `id`.
2. INPUT: Method name, params table, callback function. The bridge.send() from S24.
3. LOGIC: Implement `M.request(method, params, cb)` that: (a) generates a monotonic id (string), (b) stores `{ cb, timer }` in a pending table keyed by id, (c) sends the request via bridge.send, (d) starts a timer (rpc_timeout_ms from config) that, on expiry, removes the entry and calls cb(nil, "timeout"). Implement `M.handle_response(msg)` that looks up `msg.id` in pending table, calls the stored cb with msg.result or msg.error, cancels the timer, and removes the entry. Stale ids simply find no entry → silently dropped.
4. OUTPUT: RPC requests are correlated by id. Stale responses are silently dropped. Timeouts are handled.
5. MOCKING: Test response correlation, stale drop, timeout.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining id correlation and supersession.

subtasks.title: Notification handler for commandsChanged
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §5.4, commandsChanged is a server→client notification (no id, no reply). The on_event callback in bridge.lua receives parsed messages — those without an `id` field are notifications.
2. INPUT: Parsed JSON messages from the JSONL reader.
3. LOGIC: In the message dispatch logic, check: if msg has no `id` field and msg.method == "commandsChanged", call a registered `on_commands_changed` callback (or clear a module-level command cache). If msg has `id`, route to handle_response from S26.
4. OUTPUT: commandsChanged notifications trigger cache clearing.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining notification vs request routing.

milestones.title: Coordinate Conversion (coords.lua)
milestones.description: Implement the byte ↔ UTF-16 coordinate conversion module that translates between Neovim's byte-indexed cursor positions and pi's UTF-16 code-unit-indexed cursor positions.

tasks.title: coords.lua — byte↔UTF-16 and nvim↔pi cursor conversion
tasks.description: Implement the coordinate conversion module using Neovim's built-in vim.str_utfindex and vim.str_byteindex with the 'utf-16' encoding argument for exact conversion (no codepoint approximation needed).

subtasks.title: byte_to_utf16(line, byte_idx) and utf16_to_byte(line, utf16_idx) primitives
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/system_context.md (key discovery), Neovim 0.12 provides 3-arg forms: `vim.str_utfindex(str, 'utf-16', byte_idx)` returns exact UTF-16 code unit index, and `vim.str_byteindex(str, 'utf-16', utf16_idx)` returns exact byte index. This is MORE correct than the PRD's suggested codepoint approximation (2-arg str_utfindex). Verified: `vim.str_utfindex('héllo', 'utf-16', 3)` → 2, `vim.str_byteindex('héllo', 'utf-16', 2)` → 3. Handle edge case: byte_idx beyond string length should return the string's UTF-16 length.
2. INPUT: A Lua string (UTF-8) and a byte index (0-indexed) or UTF-16 index (0-indexed).
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/lua/pi-editor/coords.lua`. Implement `M.byte_to_utf16(line, byte_idx)` → calls `vim.str_utfindex(line, "utf-16", byte_idx)` with pcall safety. Implement `M.utf16_to_byte(line, utf16_idx)` → calls `vim.str_byteindex(line, "utf-16", utf16_idx)` with pcall safety. Both return the converted index. Clamp/handle out-of-range indices gracefully.
4. OUTPUT: Pure conversion functions that handle BMP and astral-plane characters exactly.
5. MOCKING: Test ASCII (identity), multibyte BMP (é, 日), astral (emoji 😀 = surrogate pair in UTF-16). Verify round-trip byte→utf16→byte.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining the UTF-16 vs codepoint distinction and why 3-arg form is used.

subtasks.title: nvim_to_pi_coords() and pi_to_nvim_coords() wrapper functions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/external_deps.md, Neovim cursor is `{row, col}` where row is 1-indexed and col is 0-indexed byte offset (from nvim_win_get_cursor). pi's cursorLine is 0-indexed and cursorCol is 0-indexed UTF-16. Lines from nvim_buf_get_lines are 0-indexed Lua strings.
2. INPUT: Neovim lines (array of Lua strings), cursor {row, col} (1-indexed row, 0-indexed byte col) — or pi's lines (same array), cursorLine (0-indexed), cursorCol (0-indexed UTF-16).
3. LOGIC: Implement `M.nvim_to_pi_coords(lines, row, col)`: cursorLine = row - 1, cursorCol = byte_to_utf16(lines[row], col) (col is 0-indexed byte, lines[row] is the 1-indexed line). Return {cursorLine, cursorCol}. Implement `M.pi_to_nvim_coords(lines, cursorLine, cursorCol)`: row = cursorLine + 1, byte_col = utf16_to_byte(lines[cursorLine + 1], cursorCol). Return {row, byte_col}.
4. OUTPUT: Two wrapper functions that convert full cursor coordinates between the two systems.
5. MOCKING: Test with multibyte content. Verify nvim→pi→nvim round-trip.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring with conversion table from PRD §8.

milestones.title: Completion Flow — Triggers, Accept, Tab
milestones.description: Implement the completion.lua module that triggers getSuggestions on text changes with debounce, accepts items via applyCompletion with buffer replacement and cursor positioning, and handles Tab-triggered file completion via shouldTriggerFileCompletion.

tasks.title: Completion triggers & debounce
tasks.description: Implement the trigger scheduling that fires on InsertEnter/TextChangedI/CursorMovedI with configurable debounce, extracts buffer lines and cursor position, converts coordinates, and calls getSuggestions via the bridge.

subtasks.title: Trigger scheduling with debounce via vim.defer_fn
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §7.4, triggers are InsertEnter, InsertCharPre/TextChangedI, CursorMovedI (insert). Debounce default 25ms. Per architecture/external_deps.md, use `vim.defer_fn(fn, ms)` for debounce (cancel previous timer). The completion module needs access to the bridge client and coords module.
2. INPUT: Buffer-local autocmds from S22. Config debounce_ms from setup().
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/lua/pi-editor/completion.lua`. Implement `M.refresh()` that: (a) cancels any pending debounce timer, (b) starts a new `vim.defer_fn` with debounce_ms, (c) the deferred function calls `M._do_request()`. Implement `M._do_request()` that: (a) gets lines via `nvim_buf_get_lines(0, 0, -1, false)`, (b) gets cursor via `nvim_win_get_cursor(0)`, (c) converts coords via coords.nvim_to_pi_coords, (d) calls bridge.request("getSuggestions", {lines, cursorLine, cursorCol}, callback). The callback will update the menu (placeholder for now).
4. OUTPUT: Typing triggers debounced getSuggestions RPC calls with correctly converted coordinates.
5. MOCKING: Mock bridge.request to verify correct params. Verify debounce cancels stale timers.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining the debounce and trigger logic.

subtasks.title: getSuggestions result → menu population
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: getSuggestions returns `AutocompleteSuggestions | null` where `{ items: AutocompleteItem[], prefix: string }`. AutocompleteItem is `{ value, label, description? }`. Null means no suggestions (hide menu). The items+prefix must be stored for use during accept (applyCompletion needs the prefix and item).
2. INPUT: RPC callback result from bridge.request("getSuggestions", ...).
3. LOGIC: In the getSuggestions callback: (a) if result is null or result.items is empty → close/hide menu, (b) store `current_items = result.items` and `current_prefix = result.prefix`, (c) call menu.open(result.items) (from S34/S35). Guard against stale responses (compare against latest request id if needed — bridge already drops stale ids, but check if items match current buffer state).
4. OUTPUT: Menu shows suggestions when available, hides when not.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining result handling.

tasks.title: Accept flow via applyCompletion
tasks.description: Implement the acceptance logic that sends applyCompletion to the bridge with the selected item and prefix, receives the new full buffer lines and cursor, replaces the buffer, and positions the cursor with correct byte conversion.

subtasks.title: Accept — applyCompletion RPC, replace buffer, set cursor, close menu
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §7.4 accept flow: (1) read current lines + cursor, (2) call applyCompletion(lines, cursorLine, cursorCol, selectedItem, prefix), (3) replace buffer lines via nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, result.lines), (4) position cursor: convert result.cursorCol (UTF-16) → byte via coords, then nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { result.cursorLine + 1, bytecol }), (5) close menu, stay in insert mode. Per architecture/research-pi-autocomplete.md, applyCompletion handles all insertion edge cases (trailing spaces, directories, quotes, /cmd space).
2. INPUT: The selected AutocompleteItem (from current_items), the current_prefix (from getSuggestions result). Current buffer lines + cursor.
3. LOGIC: Implement `M.accept(item)` that: (a) gets current lines + cursor, converts to pi coords, (b) calls bridge.request("applyCompletion", {lines, cursorLine, cursorCol, item, prefix}, callback), (c) in callback: nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, result.lines), convert result.cursorLine/cursorCol to nvim coords, nvim_win_set_cursor(0, {row, byte_col}), close menu, (d) use feedkeys to re-enter insert mode if needed (`vim.api.nvim_feedkeys`). The RPC is synchronous from pi's side but async on ours — the callback handles the result.
4. OUTPUT: Buffer is updated with the accepted completion and cursor is positioned correctly.
5. MOCKING: Mock bridge to verify applyCompletion is called with correct params, verify buffer replacement and cursor positioning.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining the 5-step accept flow from PRD §7.4.

tasks.title: Tab-triggered file completion (shouldTriggerFileCompletion)
tasks.description: Implement the Tab-with-no-menu-open behavior that calls shouldTriggerFileCompletion to check if file completion should be forced, then calls getSuggestions with force=true.

subtasks.title: Tab handler — shouldTriggerFileCompletion + force getSuggestions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §7.4, 'Tab with no menu open → call shouldTriggerFileCompletion; if true, call getSuggestions(..., { force = true }) and show results (matches pi's Tab).' Per architecture/research-pi-autocomplete.md, shouldTriggerFileCompletion returns false when typing a bare command like /set at start of line with no space. Per PRD §11, 'force file completion on empty line must respect shouldTriggerFileCompletion — the plugin must not bypass it.' Per editor.ts:2150-2160, when force is true and items.length===1 and explicitTab, pi auto-applies immediately.
2. INPUT: The current buffer state (lines, cursor). Whether the menu is currently open.
3. LOGIC: Implement `M.handle_tab()` that: (a) if menu is open → call M.accept(selected_item) (Tab accepts), (b) if menu is NOT open → get lines+cursor, convert to pi coords, call bridge.request("shouldTriggerFileCompletion", {lines, cursorLine, cursorCol}, cb), (c) in callback: if result is true → call bridge.request("getSuggestions", {..., force=true}, cb2) and show results, (d) if result is false → insert a literal Tab character (`vim.api.nvim_feedkeys` with "\t").
4. OUTPUT: Tab triggers file completion when appropriate, accepts when menu is open, or inserts Tab when shouldTrigger is false.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining the three Tab behaviors.

milestones.title: Floating Completion Menu (menu.lua)
milestones.description: Implement the dependency-free floating completion popup that renders suggestion items in two columns (label, description), handles navigation keys, and auto-positions near the cursor with window-edge clamping.

tasks.title: menu.lua — popup creation, rendering & positioning
tasks.description: Create the floating window, render completion items with label/description columns and highlight, and position it relative to the cursor with clamping to screen edges.

subtasks.title: Floating window creation with cursor-relative positioning & edge clamping
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/external_deps.md, use `vim.api.nvim_open_win(buf, false, config)` with config `{ relative="cursor", row=1, col=0, width=W, height=H, style="minimal", border="rounded" or "none", focusable=false }`. Width should accommodate label+description columns. Height clamped to `config.menu.max_height` and number of items. Position must clamp to screen edges: if cursor is near bottom, show above; if near right edge, shift left. Use `vim.api.nvim_win_set_option(win, "wrap", false)`. Create a dedicated scratch buffer for the menu.
2. INPUT: Array of AutocompleteItem `{ value, label, description? }`. Config `menu.max_height` and `menu.border`.
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/lua/pi-editor/menu.lua`. Implement `M.open(items)`: (a) if already open, update contents, (b) create or reuse scratch buffer, (c) compute display lines (see S35 for rendering), (d) compute width (max label+desc+gap, clamped to screen width), (e) compute height (min(#items, max_height)), (f) compute position with edge clamping using `vim.fn.screenrow()`, `vim.fn.screencol()`, `vim.o.columns`, `vim.o.lines`, (g) open floating window, (h) track selected index.
4. OUTPUT: A floating window appears near the cursor showing completion items, clamped to screen edges.
5. MOCKING: Test with various item counts, cursor positions (top/bottom/left/right edges).
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining positioning math and clamping logic.

subtasks.title: Item rendering — two-column label/description, highlight selected row
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §7.5, render 'two columns — label (left) and description (right, truncated).' Use nvim_buf_set_lines for content and nvim_buf_add_highlight for the selected row highlight. Create a namespace via vim.api.nvim_create_namespace.
2. INPUT: AutocompleteItem array and selected index.
3. LOGIC: Implement `M.render(items, selected_idx)` that: (a) builds display lines: for each item, format as `label .. padding .. description` where label is left-justified to the max label width and description is truncated to remaining width, (b) set buffer lines via nvim_buf_set_lines, (c) clear existing highlights, (d) highlight selected row: nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, ns, "PmenuSel", selected_idx, 0, -1), (e) optionally highlight label vs description with different groups (e.g., "Pmenu" for label, comment-like for description).
4. OUTPUT: Menu buffer shows formatted items with the selected row highlighted.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining the two-column layout.

tasks.title: menu.lua — navigation, key handling & lifecycle
tasks.description: Implement menu navigation (next/prev/select/dismiss), key handling while the menu is open, and auto-close behavior on InsertLeave or cursor movement out of the completion prefix.

subtasks.title: Navigation & key handling — C-N/C-P/Up/Down, C-E dismiss, Tab/C-Y/CR accept
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §7.5, keys active while menu is up: <C-N>/<Down> next, <C-P>/<Up> prev, <C-E> dismiss, <Tab>/<C-Y>/<CR> accept. These are buffer-local keymaps set in ftplugin (S22) that route to menu functions. The menu is NOT a modal — the user stays in insert mode and the keymaps intercept these specific keys. Per architecture/external_deps.md, use vim.keymap.set with buffer-local scope.
2. INPUT: The selected index and item count.
3. LOGIC: Implement `M.next()` (selected = (selected + 1) % #items, re-render), `M.prev()` (selected = (selected - 2 + #items) % #items + 1, re-render), `M.dismiss()` (close window, clear state), `M.get_selected()` (return items[selected]). The accept is handled by completion.lua's accept() (S32) which calls M.get_selected() then closes. Wire these to the ftplugin keymaps. The navigation wraps around.
4. OUTPUT: User can navigate, dismiss, and select items via keyboard while staying in insert mode.
5. MOCKING: Test next/prev wraparound, dismiss, get_selected.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining each navigation function.

subtasks.title: Auto-close on InsertLeave, CursorMoved out of prefix, buffer change
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §7.5, 'close on InsertLeave, CursorMoved out of prefix, or buffer write.' The prefix is the text before the cursor that getSuggestions matched. If the user moves the cursor to a different line or deletes past the prefix start, the menu should close.
2. INPUT: Current cursor position vs. the position when suggestions were requested.
3. LOGIC: Register autocmds (buffer-local, in the ftplugin or dynamically when menu opens): (a) InsertLeave → M.dismiss(), (b) CursorMovedI → check if cursor is still on the same line and within or after the prefix; if not → M.dismiss(). Also close the menu window when the buffer is written or the tab/window changes.
4. OUTPUT: Menu closes automatically on mode change, cursor escape, or buffer events.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining auto-close triggers.

milestones.title: Autosave & Exit Handling
milestones.description: Implement the autosave-on-exit behavior that ensures pi reads the latest prompt content when the editor exits, and clean teardown of the bridge connection.

tasks.title: Autosave on VimLeavePre/ExitPre & bridge teardown
tasks.description: Implement the exit handlers that write the buffer to the temp file if modified (so pi reads the latest content on status 0 exit), send bye to the bridge, and close the socket connection.

subtasks.title: VimLeavePre/ExitPre — autosave if modified, send bye, close connection
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §11 (critical edge case): 'pi reads the file only after the editor exits with status 0. The plugin MUST autosave the buffer on VimLeavePre/ExitPre when modified. Without this a user who types and quits with :q silently loses their prompt.' Per PRD §10.5, autosave_on_exit defaults to true. Per PRD §5.4, bye method returns {ok:true} for graceful disconnect. Also handle BufWriteCmd so that :w triggers a write to the temp file.
2. INPUT: The buffer's modified flag (`vim.bo.modified`). The temp file path (from buffer name). The bridge client from S24.
3. LOGIC: Implement `M.on_exit()` registered for VimLeavePre and ExitPre: (a) if config.autosave_on_exit and vim.bo.modified → `vim.cmd("write")` or `vim.api.nvim_buf_call(bufnr, function() vim.cmd("silent! write") end)`, (b) if bridge is connected → send bye notification, close pipe, (c) do NOT throw — wrap in pcall. Also implement BufWriteCmd handler that writes to the temp file (so :w works normally).
4. OUTPUT: Buffer is saved on exit, bridge connection is cleanly closed.
5. MOCKING: Test modified vs unmodified buffer, verify write is called, verify bye is sent.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring with WARNING comment about the lost-prompt risk.

backlog.title: Polish, Quality & Documentation
backlog.description: Add resilience (silent degradation, error handling), refine timing (debounce, timeout, supersession), implement checkhealth diagnostics, and sync all changeset-level documentation (vimdoc, READMEs).

milestones.title: Resilience & UX Polish
milestones.description: Make the plugin robust against all failure modes: missing socket, bad handshake, pi process death, fd not installed, and configuration errors. Ensure silent degradation never blocks startup.

tasks.title: Silent degradation — connect fail, bad handshake, process death
tasks.description: Implement graceful failure handling so that any bridge connection failure degrades silently to a normal buffer with at most a single vim.notify.

subtasks.title: Graceful failure — degrade to normal buffer with single notify
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §11, 'If connect() fails or hello errors, the plugin must degrade silently to a normal buffer (no completion), optionally with a single vim.notify the first time. Never block startup or spam.' Also: 'pi process dies while editor open: the socket closes; the plugin detects EOF on the pipe, stops completion, and may notify once.'
2. INPUT: Error conditions from bridge.connect(), handshake, and pipe EOF.
3. LOGIC: Implement a `notified` flag per session. On any bridge error (connect fail, handshake fail, pipe EOF), if not notified yet → `vim.notify("pi-editor: bridge unavailable, completion disabled", vim.log.levels.WARN)` and set notified=true. Set `M.active = false` to short-circuit completion triggers. The buffer remains a normal editable markdown buffer.
4. OUTPUT: Any bridge failure results in graceful degradation — buffer still works for editing, just without completion.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining the degradation strategy.

tasks.title: Timing refinement — debounce, timeout, supersession tuning
tasks.description: Refine the debounce, RPC timeout, and stale-request supersession to match pi's timing semantics and ensure responsive but not spammable completion.

subtasks.title: Configurable debounce, RPC timeout, and stale-response supersession
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §5.5, client debounce default 25ms for slash/path, 0ms extra for @ (fd is async). RPC timeout default 2000ms. The bridge already drops stale responses by id (S26). Per architecture/research-pi-autocomplete.md, pi's editor uses 20ms debounce for attachment triggers and 0ms for forced Tab. The plugin should respect config.debounce_ms and config.rpc_timeout_ms.
2. INPUT: Config values from setup().
3. LOGIC: (a) Use config.debounce_ms in the trigger scheduling (S30), (b) use config.rpc_timeout_ms in bridge.request timeout (S26), (c) verify that rapid typing generates only one active request (supersession works end-to-end), (d) add a small additional debounce (or 0ms) for @-triggered requests to match pi's attachment debounce pattern.
4. OUTPUT: Completion feels responsive without flooding the bridge with stale requests.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining timing configuration.

tasks.title: commandsChanged cache invalidation
tasks.description: Ensure that when the bridge sends a commandsChanged notification (on reload/new/resume/fork), the plugin clears any cached command data and re-queries fresh suggestions.

subtasks.title: Clear caches and re-query on commandsChanged notification
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §6.2, session_start with reason reload re-captures the provider (commands may have changed). The bridge sends commandsChanged notification. Per PRD §11, 'Reload during an open editor: session_start {reason:"reload"} re-captures the provider and re-advertises. The open editor's existing connection stays valid.' The plugin should clear any local command cache and refresh.
2. INPUT: commandsChanged notification from S27.
3. LOGIC: On commandsChanged: (a) clear current_items and current_prefix, (b) close the menu if open, (c) trigger a fresh completion refresh if the user is mid-typing.
4. OUTPUT: Command list stays fresh across reloads.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining the cache invalidation flow.

tasks.title: :checkhealth pi-editor module
tasks.description: Implement a health check module that verifies Neovim version, PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE presence, bridge connectivity, fd availability, and reports helpful diagnostics.

subtasks.title: health.lua — version, env, socket, fd checks
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/external_deps.md, checkhealth uses `vim.health.start()`, `vim.health.ok()`, `vim.health.warn()`, `vim.health.error()`. The module must be at `lua/pi-editor/health.lua` and export a `check()` function. Run via `:checkhealth pi-editor`.
2. INPUT: Neovim version, PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE env var, config values.
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/lua/pi-editor/health.lua` with `M.check()` that: (a) checks Neovim version >= 0.10 (ok/warn), (b) checks if PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE is set (if set, parse and show transport/path; if not, warn that plugin is dormant), (c) if env var is set, verify the socket path exists, (d) check if bridge is connected, (e) report fdAvailable from descriptor (warn if false — @file completion won't work), (f) check that vim.uv is available.
4. OUTPUT: `:checkhealth pi-editor` shows a diagnostic report.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] The health.lua IS the documentation for this subtask.

subtasks.title: Write doc/pi-editor.txt vimdoc with commands, options, keymaps, troubleshooting
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Vimdoc format uses tags like `*pi-editor.txt*`, `*pi-editor-setup*`, section headers with `=` lines, and code blocks with `>` markers. The doc should cover: overview, installation (lazy.nvim, manual), setup() options table, keymaps table, commands (:PiSubmit if implemented), troubleshooting (bridge unavailable, fd missing, lost prompt warning), and known limitations.

subtasks.title: Write/update README.md for both plugin and extension
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: The project has two components — extension (TypeScript) and plugin (Lua). A top-level README.md should serve as the project overview and link to both. Per PRD §1 (TL;DR), summarize: pi extension captures live AutocompleteProvider, serves over Unix socket via process.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE, Neovim plugin connects and renders completions through a dependency-free menu.
2. INPUT: All implemented features across P1-P4.
3. LOGIC: Create/update top-level `README.md` with: (a) project title and one-paragraph summary (from PRD TL;DR), (b) architecture diagram (ASCII, from PRD §3), (c) features list (slash commands, @file, path completion, Tab force), (d) quickstart (install extension + plugin + set EDITOR), (e) installation sections for both components, (f) configuration section, (g) how it works (process.env inheritance discovery), (h) known limitations, (i) optional integrations (blink.cmp, nvim-cmp), (j) license. Also update `extension/README.md` (from S18) if needed to stay in sync.
4. OUTPUT: Comprehensive README that onboards a new user from zero to working completion.
5. DOCS: [Mode B] This IS the changeset-level documentation subtask.

backlog.title: Optional Integrations
backlog.description: Implement optional completion-engine integrations (blink.cmp source, nvim-cmp source) for users who prefer their existing completion plugin over the built-in menu, plus the NVIM_APPNAME minimal-config optimization.

milestones.title: Completion Engine Sources & Optimization
milestones.description: Ship opt-in modules that integrate with blink.cmp and nvim-cmp, reusing the same bridge + applyCompletion path. Document the NVIM_APPNAME optimization for faster Neovim startup.

tasks.title: blink.cmp source module
tasks.description: Implement a blink.cmp source that bridges pi's getSuggestions into blink's completion pipeline, mapping AutocompleteItems to LSP CompletionItems and using applyCompletion for acceptance.

subtasks.title: blink_source.lua — source.new, get_trigger_characters, get_completions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/external_deps.md, blink.cmp source contract: `source.new(opts)` returns source object. `source:enabled()` returns bool. `source:get_trigger_characters()` returns string[]. `source:get_completions(ctx, callback)` calls callback with `{ items = { { label, kind, ... } }, is_incomplete_backward, is_incomplete_forward }`. MUST call callback at least once. Return a cancel function for long-running requests. blink.cmp mutates items — deepcopy if caching. Items are LSP CompletionItem-shaped. Registration via user's blink.cmp config: `providers = { ['pi-editor'] = { module = 'pi-editor.blink_source' } }`. IMPORTANT: For acceptance, use the `execute` method to call applyCompletion since blink's default textEdit won't match pi's insertion rules.
2. INPUT: The bridge client (from P2.M5), coords module (from P2.M6), AutocompleteItems from getSuggestions.
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/lua/pi-editor/blink_source.lua` with: (a) `source.new(opts)` → setmetatable, store reference to pi-editor bridge, (b) `source:enabled()` → return `vim.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE ~= nil and require("pi-editor").bridge ~= nil`, (c) `source:get_trigger_characters()` → `{ "/", "@" }`, (d) `source:get_completions(ctx, callback)` → extract lines+cursor from ctx, convert coords, call bridge.request("getSuggestions", ...), in callback map AutocompleteItems to LSP CompletionItems `{ label = item.label, detail = item.description, kind = CompletionItemKind.Text }`, call blink callback. Return cancel function. (e) `source:execute(ctx, item, callback, default)` → call pi-editor's accept flow (applyCompletion), call callback().
4. OUTPUT: A valid blink.cmp source that users can register in their config.
5. MOCKING: Verify source interface compliance, verify get_completions calls bridge.request with correct params.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining how to register the source in blink.cmp config.

tasks.title: nvim-cmp source module
tasks.description: Implement an nvim-cmp source that bridges pi's getSuggestions into nvim-cmp's completion pipeline.

subtasks.title: cmp_source.lua — source.new, get_trigger_characters, complete
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/external_deps.md, nvim-cmp source contract: `source.new()` returns source object. `source:is_available()` returns bool. `source:get_trigger_characters()` returns string[]. `source:complete(params, callback)` calls callback with LSP CompletionItem array. `params` has `context`, `offset`, `completion_context`. Registration via `require('cmp').register_source('pi-editor', source.new())`. Items are LSP CompletionItem-shaped. For acceptance, nvim-cmp uses textEdit or insertText — but pi's applyCompletion handles complex insertion, so use execute method or custom confirm.
2. INPUT: The bridge client, coords module, AutocompleteItems.
3. LOGIC: Create `plugin/lua/pi-editor/cmp_source.lua` with: (a) `source.new()` → setmetatable, (b) `source:is_available()` → `vim.env.PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE ~= nil and require("pi-editor").bridge ~= nil`, (c) `source:get_trigger_characters()` → `{ "/", "@" }`, (d) `source:complete(params, callback)` → extract lines+cursor from params.context, convert coords, call bridge.request("getSuggestions", ...), map items to `{ label = item.label, detail = item.description }`, call callback. (e) For acceptance: override the confirm behavior or document that users should use the built-in menu for full applyCompletion fidelity.
4. OUTPUT: A valid nvim-cmp source that users can register.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Lua docstring explaining registration and the acceptance caveat.

tasks.title: NVIM_APPNAME minimal-config optimization
tasks.description: Document and optionally implement the NVIM_APPNAME optimization where the bridge extension sets process.env.NVIM_APPNAME to a minimal Neovim config that loads only pi-editor.nvim for faster startup.

subtasks.title: Document & implement optional NVIM_APPNAME env var in bridge extension
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per PRD §10.4, 'the bridge extension may additionally set process.env.NVIM_APPNAME = "pi-editor" (documented opt-in), and the user maintains a tiny ~/.config/pi-editor/ that loads only pi-editor.nvim. This is an optional optimization, not required.' Neovim reads NVIM_APPNAME to determine config directory (~/.config/$NVIM_APPNAME/).
2. INPUT: Config option (opt-in flag in extension or plugin).
3. LOGIC: Add an optional `nvim_appname` config option to the bridge extension. If set (e.g., to "pi-editor"), the extension writes `process.env.NVIM_APPNAME = nvim_appname` alongside PI_EDITOR_BRIDGE in session_start. Document in README that the user should create a minimal config at ~/.config/pi-editor/ that loads only pi-editor.nvim. Also document that this is purely an optimization.
4. OUTPUT: When enabled, Neovim starts with a minimal config for faster editor launch.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the NVIM_APPNAME option, and Mode B update to README in S44.
